components.gap: The success condition requires stating the warranted assignment contrast AND the additional premise for a mechanism claim. The first half is met (factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 692-726; 077 404-466). The second is not: the text proves the reflection mechanism is not identified (thm:p15-factorial-mechanism) and then lists only categories of further evidence plus unspecified 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations' (736-741). The same deferral recurs at 077:449-450 ('needs the additional evidence'), 075:661-662 ('needs further premises again') and P19:667-670. Nowhere is the premise itself stated. An example of such a premise is a structural restriction that excludes the competing effort path that separates the two models of the theorem, or a stated condition under which the reflection variable's intervention effect is identified. The chapter's own opening claim (lines 12-13) to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism' is therefore not delivered. The failure condition does not hold, because no factorial coefficient is called proof of the mechanism.

defect_observations.observation: The opening promise to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is an effect of assignment or an identified causal mechanism' is met only for assignment. The final section (728-746) proves nonidentification of the mechanism and lists evidence categories, but it states no condition under which a mechanism is identified. This is the basis of the C04 partial verdict.

This is a silent departure from the held source. NIST sec. 5.3.3.4.4 (PDF p. 1345) says the 6=12345, 7=135, 8=245 design confounds 23 of 28 two-factor interactions, leaving 12, 14, 23, 27 and 34. The body states that 24 are aliased, that 12, 14, 23 and 34 are clear, and lists 27=46. Annex lines 332-337 derive 27=46 from I=2467. Neither place flags that it corrects the source the chapter says it retains. The handbook's count follows from the defining relation. This is a reader and fidelity note, not a coverage failure.

In the five-level Hyper-Graeco-Latin display, row 3 has E13. The held source's letter representation (sec. 5.3.3.2.3, PDF p. 1318) prints E31. E13 agrees with the source's own tabular run (3,4,1,3,5). The correction is not flagged.

The toc tag claims sections 174.5-174.8, but this chapter has no section for 174.5 or 174.6. The 174.6 material (fractions, defining relations, aliasing, estimability) lives in the pre-existing chapter sec:p15-factorial-inference (sec:p15-factorial-estimability, -fractions, -half). It is reached from here only through the cross-reference at lines 21-27.

'The same calculation with the factors exchanged proves the formulas for B' is a 'similarly' step. It is not counted against C01: Delta_B=2beta_B is independently proved by annex:p15.factorial.walsh (lines 234-240), and B's conditional effects are given explicitly in the retained example (body line 105).

Line 552, 'The last two analysis columns x3, x1x2 coincide', reads ambiguously against the displayed table at 542-547. That table's last two columns are the alternative x3 columns (+x1x2 and -x1x2), which are negatives of each other. The coincidence is still visible in the x1x2 and x3=+x1x2 columns. Separately, the source's textual 2^(6-2) illustration in sec. 5.3.3.4.3 (5=123 giving 15=23, PDF p. 1340) is not retained. It is not an example matrix, and two-factor-to-two-factor aliasing is retained through the eight-factor examples, so it is not counted.
